01 / ABOUT

A bridge between
theory and practice.

I am a PhD student in financial mathematics, actuarial risk and stochastic modelling. My doctoral work is hosted by BPCE Vie in an industrial partnership with CERMICS at École nationale des ponts et chaussées and LIRSA at Le Cnam.

I am supervised by Benjamin Jourdain and Stéphane Loisel, with Adrien Helary as my industry supervisor. I trained in mathematics and data science at CentraleSupélec and completed the Mathematics of Randomness master’s programme at Université Paris-Saclay.

02 / RESEARCH

Understanding risk
at the intersection.

My thesis studies the stochastic evolution of life-insurance savings and rare events affecting policyholders, with an emphasis on accurate risk estimates that are practical to compute.

DOCTORAL PROJECT2026 — PRESENT

Stochastic estimation of life-insurance policyholders’ savings and rare events

Insurers must model both changing financial markets and decisions such as surrendering a policy. Simulating policyholder behaviour within each market scenario makes asset–liability modelling more realistic, but also much more expensive. I investigate nested Monte Carlo and multilevel Monte Carlo methods to make estimates of the best estimate and Solvency Capital Requirement more efficient, while studying their convergence when the quantities of interest are irregular.

∿

Policyholder dynamics

Stochastic models of savings, death and surrender decisions, including large withdrawals that standard portfolio averages can miss.

Σ

Efficient risk estimation

Nested simulation and MLMC for asset–liability models, with attention to computational cost, convergence, best estimates and SCR.

◌

Correlated rare events

How market stress, sustainability shocks and AI-influenced financial advice may make many policyholders act together.

This is a summary of the research programme; results and publications will be added as the work develops.
